What is the reliability assessment on overweight or obese youth (12 to 17, self-reported BMI) in Région de Laval, Quebec, 2021/2022 (percent)?
response_text:
**Marked "E" — use with caution.**

The estimate is **38.9%** (95% CI: 26.7–52.7), and all three rows carry `STATUS = "E"`, which the symbol legend defines as *"use with caution."*

What that reflects in the data itself:
- The CI spans **26 percentage points** — the high bound is nearly double the low bound.
- The relative width (~67% of the point estimate) is characteristic of a high coefficient of variation, typical of a small subgroup: youth 12–17 within a single health region.

Contrast with the other Laval indicators in this extract, which carry no quality flag: adult obesity 28.9% (25.3–32.8), arthritis 16.5% (14.3–18.9), diabetes 8.7% (7.1–10.8) — all with much tighter bounds.

Practical reading: 38.9% is directional, not precise. It's publishable but shouldn't anchor a point comparison against another region or another cycle unless the difference is large — with a CI that wide, most such comparisons won't be statistically distinguishable. Note also that it's a *combined* overweight-or-obese measure and self-reported, so it isn't comparable to the adult row, which is adjusted self-reported obesity only.
